summary: 60 ft steel tower in the Bremerton watershed, Kitsap County, WA; origin disputed (Navy vs state fire lookout), 1940s; abandoned 1950s; found standing again in the 2000s; restricted access.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower; WillhiteWeb describes two planks near the top used to align 16-inch naval guns, an account not independently verified
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s and presumed destroyed until found standing in the 2000s. Wikipedia says it still stands; the firelookout.com page gives only 'Abandoned 1950s'.
facts.agency: State: Washington Division of Forestry/DNR (per firelookout.com); the naval origin is disputed

staffing.status: fire lookout staffed in the 1940s; Charles R. Siegel Jr. about 1943; tended until at least 1944

access.note: Inside the City of Bremerton watershed on non-public government land. Wikipedia says the mountain is inaccessible to the general public and visiting is highly discouraged.

visit.trail_note: No road leads directly to the summit (TrailChick). Not recommended: non-public land in a city watershed. No route is given in this record.

events.note: Firelookout.com gives 1940; TrailChick, WillhiteWeb and Wikipedia say the 1940s or early 1940s. WillhiteWeb says likely built by the U.S. Navy; origin disputed.
Charles R. Siegel Jr. worked as a fire lookout here about 1943, per a friend's recollection on WillhiteWeb and TrailChick
Abandoned in the 1950s per firelookout.com; the decade is all the source gives, so 1950 is a placeholder year
Presumed destroyed for a time, then found standing again in the early 2000s; exact year not given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.org's list and Wikipedia say standing; firelookout.com's page gives only 'Abandoned 1950s'. Treated as standing, with the abandonment and rediscovery noted in status_note.
1,360 ft (414.5 m) is the site elevation given by firelookout.com and TrailChick. Wikipedia's 1,378 ft (420 m) is the elevation of the summit. The record's 414.5 m is kept.

Firelookout.com lists the Washington Division of Forestry/DNR, which supports the record's 'State'. WillhiteWeb and Wikipedia describe a likely Navy origin. Both are reported; the builder is not settled.

notes_for_editor: Read: firelookout.com, TrailChick (first 3,000 of about 5,200 chars), WillhiteWeb (first 3,000 of about 4,500 chars; the access section after that was not read), Wikipedia (excerpt), the firelookout.org list (Kitsap line), and the weebly index (menu only). Not read: SummitPost, the Kitsap History Museum, Grokipedia; those appeared only as search snippets and are not cited. The brief's note that firelookout.com's map omits Kitsap was not checked. Origin is contested (Navy per WillhiteWeb, TrailChick's 'some say' and Wikipedia's 'naval observation tower'; state fire lookout per firelookout.com and Wikipedia's 'primary use'). Build date differs: 1940 (firelookout.com) vs 1940s (TrailChick, WillhiteWeb) vs early 1940s (Wikipedia). TrailChick gives its visit as spring 2017 in the text and 2/24/18 in the header; that is not used. The record's access 'unknown' is set to restricted from Wikipedia. The Siegel material is a friend's recollection on WillhiteWeb. Route details from TrailChick are deliberately left out. No photos were added.
